examples.question_text:
Two runners record their $100$ m times in seconds.
Ava: $16,18,17,20,19$
Ben: $15,19,21,16,18,17$
Calculate each runner's mean time, correct to $1$ decimal place, and range. Who is faster on average, and who is more consistent?
examples.solution_text:
Ava's mean:
$\begin{aligned}\overline{x}_{A}&=\frac{16+18+17+20+19}{5}\\&=18.0\text{ s}\end{aligned}$
Ben's mean:
$\begin{aligned}\overline{x}_{B}&=\frac{15+19+21+16+18+17}{6}\\&\approx17.7\text{ s}\end{aligned}$
Ben is faster on average because his mean time is lower.
Ava's range:
$\begin{aligned}R_A&=20-16\\&=4\text{ s}\end{aligned}$
Ben's range:
$\begin{aligned}R_B&=21-15\\&=6\text{ s}\end{aligned}$
Ava is more consistent because her range is smaller.

examples.question_text:
Three groups complete a puzzle. The table shows their completion times.

| Group | Mean time (s) | Range (s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | 26 | 12 |
| B | 22 | 16 |
| C | 34 | 8 |

Leo says Group C did best because it has the greatest mean. Explain his mistake, identify the fastest group on average, and order the groups from most consistent to least consistent.
examples.solution_text:
A shorter completion time is better. Group C has the highest mean time, $34$ s, so it is slowest on average.
Group B is fastest on average because it has the lowest mean time, $22$ s.
For consistency, compare the ranges: $8<12<16$.
From most consistent to least consistent: C, A, B.

examples.question_text:
The heights of five basketball players and six gymnasts are recorded.
Basketball players: $198,193,202,196,191$ cm
Gymnasts: $155,149,161,157,147,159$ cm
Find and compare the median heights.
examples.solution_text:
Basketball heights in ascending order:
$191,193,196,198,202$
The middle value is the third value, so the median is $196$ cm.
Gymnast heights in ascending order:
$147,149,155,157,159,161$
There are two middle values.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Median}&=\frac{155+157}{2}\\&=156\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$
The basketball players have the higher median height: $196$ cm compared with $156$ cm.

examples.question_text:
Two stalls record the numbers of hot dogs sold in five one-hour periods.
Stall A: $14,16,16,18,21$
Stall B: $17,18,19,20,21$
Find the mean, median, mode and range for each stall. Compare typical hourly sales and consistency.
examples.solution_text:
Both lists are already in ascending order.
Stall A:
$\begin{aligned}\overline{x}_A&=\frac{14+16+16+18+21}{5}\\&=17\\\text{Median}_A&=16\\\text{Mode}_A&=16\\R_A&=21-14\\&=7\end{aligned}$
Stall B:
$\begin{aligned}\overline{x}_B&=\frac{17+18+19+20+21}{5}\\&=19\\\text{Median}_B&=19\\R_B&=21-17\\&=4\end{aligned}$
Stall B has no mode because every value occurs once.
Stall B sells more hot dogs per hour on average according to both the mean and median. It is also more consistent because its range is smaller.

examples.question_text:
Two students record their marks on five maths tests.
Nina: $58,62,64,66,70$
Omar: $44,54,64,74,84$
Show that their mean marks are equal. Use the range to compare their consistency.
examples.solution_text:
Nina's mean:
$\begin{aligned}\overline{x}_N&=\frac{58+62+64+66+70}{5}\\&=64\end{aligned}$
Omar's mean:
$\begin{aligned}\overline{x}_O&=\frac{44+54+64+74+84}{5}\\&=64\end{aligned}$
Their mean marks are equal.
Nina's range:
$\begin{aligned}R_N&=70-58\\&=12\end{aligned}$
Omar's range:
$\begin{aligned}R_O&=84-44\\&=40\end{aligned}$
Nina's marks are more consistent because her range is smaller.

examples.question_text:
Two students record their marks on five maths tests.
Priya: $42,44,45,46,73$
Zac: $46,47,48,49,50$
Find each student's mean and median. Which student has the higher mean, and which has the higher median?
examples.solution_text:
Both lists are already in ascending order.
Priya:
$\begin{aligned}\overline{x}_P&=\frac{42+44+45+46+73}{5}\\&=50\\\text{Median}_P&=45\end{aligned}$
Zac:
$\begin{aligned}\overline{x}_Z&=\frac{46+47+48+49+50}{5}\\&=48\\\text{Median}_Z&=48\end{aligned}$
Priya has the higher mean: $50$ compared with $48$.
Zac has the higher median: $48$ compared with $45$.
The comparison depends on which measure of centre is used.

examples.derivation: Ava: total 90, mean 90/5 = 18.0 s, range 20 − 16 = 4 s. Ben: total 106, mean 106/6 ≈ 17.7 s, range 21 − 15 = 6 s. Ben has the lower mean time; Ava has the smaller range.
Mean times satisfy 22 < 26 < 34, so B is fastest and C slowest on average. Ranges satisfy 8 < 12 < 16, giving consistency order C, A, B.
Sorted basketball heights: 191, 193, 196, 198, 202; median 196 cm. Sorted gymnast heights: 147, 149, 155, 157, 159, 161; median (155 + 157)/2 = 156 cm. Basketball players have the higher median.

Stall A: total 85, mean 17, median 16, mode 16, range 7. Stall B: total 95, mean 19, median 19, no repeated values and therefore no mode, range 4. B has higher mean and median sales and a smaller range.
Nina and Omar each have total 320 and mean 320/5 = 64. Nina's range is 70 − 58 = 12; Omar's is 84 − 44 = 40. Nina is more consistent.
Priya: total 250, mean 50, middle value 45. Zac: total 240, mean 48, middle value 48. Priya has the higher mean; Zac has the higher median.
